editorial:
Imagine a world where a former geisha becomes the best fighter pilot in the army to get revenge on a giant space monster. That is exactly what you get here. The movie follows Dan, who is on a mission to kill Bemurasu, a creature that eats nuclear waste and killed her fiancé. It sounds like a serious war movie, but it is actually a wild comedy. The twist is that every time Dan attacks the monster, she feels a strange sense of pleasure. It turns the whole 'save the world' trope on its head and makes for a really weird and funny experience.

You will love how the movie doesn't take itself seriously. The acting is campy and the special effects feel like a throwback to old monster movies, which adds to the charm. While the plot is a bit repetitive, the humor keeps you moving forward. If you are in the mood for something totally off-beat, you should definitely check this out. You can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the colorful effects, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick laugh with friends on a Friday night.
endingExplained: In the end, Dan finally faces off against Bemurasu in a huge battle. She uses her strange feelings of pleasure to fuel her attacks, eventually overpowering the monster. She saves the planet, but the movie wraps up by showing that her bond with the monster was more about her own emotional release than just a fight. It ends on a light note, proving that love and weirdness can save the day.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves campy monster movies and weird Japanese humor.
